body.body: ### SUMMARY `load_configs_from_directory()` parsed the example bundle's `metadata.yaml` with `yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.Loader)` (suppressed with `# noqa: S506`). `yaml.Loader` constructs arbitrary Python objects from tags such as `!!python/object/apply`, so the parse is a deserialisation sink for any directory whose contents are attacker-influenced. The loader is now `yaml.safe_load`, matching what the rest of the importer already uses (`superset/commands/importers/v1/utils.py:load_yaml`). `SafeLoader` still resolves the implicit types the exporter emits — importantly `!!timestamp`, so the unquoted ISO timestamp in `metadata.yaml` continues to deserialise to the same tz-aware `datetime` that `MetadataSchema.timestamp` expects, and re-dumps identically. Unknown tags now raise `yaml.constructor.ConstructorError` (a `yaml.YAMLError`) instead of being constructed. The `# noqa: S506` suppression is removed, not moved. ```diff - metadata = yaml.load(contents.get(METADATA_FILE_NAME, "{}"), Loader=yaml.Loader) # noqa: S506 + metadata = yaml.safe_load(contents.get(METADATA_FILE_NAME, "{}")) ``` Two tests were added to `tests/unit_tests/examples/utils_test.py`: `..._rejects_python_object_tags` (the regression test — with the old loader the `!!python/object/apply:os.getcwd` tag is *executed* during parsing) and `..._parses_legitimate_metadata`, which pins the timestamp/`type`-stripping behaviour so the tightened loader is shown not to break legitimate bundles. ### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS Before the fix (source change reverted, test present): ``` $ python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/examples/utils_test.py -q -k python_object_tags > with pytest.raises(yaml.YAMLError): E Failed: DID NOT RAISE 1 failed, 5 deselected, 1 warning in 1.27s ``` After the fix (full file): ``` $ python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/examples/utils_test.py -q ...... [100%] 6 passed, 1 warning in 0.76s ``` `ruff check superset/examples/utils.py tests/unit_tests/examples/utils_test.py` passes. ### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION - [x] Has associated issue: Closes #7 - [ ] Required feature flags: - [ ] Changes UI - [ ] Includes DB Migration (follow approval process in [SIP-59](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/13351)) - [ ] Migration is atomic, supports rollback & is backwards-compatible - [ ] Confirm DB migration upgrade and downgrade tested - [ ] Runtime estimates and downtime expectations provided - [ ] Introduces new feature or API - [ ] Removes existing feature or API Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f617079e216a4537bd4a15a07fa68a58 ---

body.body: ### SUMMARY `superset/security/session_invalidation.py` compares a timezone-aware "now" (the session's `_login_at`) against `sessions_invalidated_at`, a **naive** UTC `DateTime` column. `_as_utc_timestamp` treats a naive value as UTC precisely because `datetime.timestamp()` on a naive datetime interprets it in the process local zone — if the helper didn't force UTC, the epoch would skew by the local UTC offset under a non-UTC `TZ` and sessions would be invalidated early or never. That invariant previously rested only on a docstring. This adds unit tests that pin it. No production module is modified. New test `test_naive_utc_matches_aware_utc_under_non_utc_tz` (parametrized over `America/Los_Angeles`, `Asia/Kolkata`, `Europe/Berlin`, `Pacific/Chatham` — east/west of UTC plus a fractional-hour zone) sets the process `TZ` via a `process_tz` fixture (`os.environ["TZ"]` + `time.tzset()`, restored on teardown so the zone doesn't leak into later tests) and asserts: - `_as_utc_timestamp(naive) == aware.timestamp()` - `_as_utc_timestamp(naive) == _as_utc_timestamp(aware)` - the `is_session_invalidated` boundary (just-before invalidated, just-after valid) holds, and the naive column and its aware equivalent invalidate identically. A sanity assertion (`time.timezone != 0 or time.altzone != 0`) confirms the chosen zone really is offset from UTC in-process, so the skew guard is actually exercised. The production behaviour is correct as documented; no change to it was needed. ### BEFORE/AFTER SCREENSHOTS OR ANIMATED GIF N/A ### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS ```bash python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/security -q ``` Result: `244 passed` (was 240; +4 new parametrized cases). `ruff check` on the changed file passes. ### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION Closes #9 - [x] Has associated issue: #9 - [ ] Required feature flags: - [ ] Changes UI - [ ] Includes DB Migration (follow approval process in [SIP-59](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/13351)) - [ ] Migration is atomic, supports rollback & is backwards-compatible - [ ] Confirm DB migration upgrade and downgrade tested - [ ] Runtime estimates and downtime expectations provided - [ ] Introduces new feature or API - [ ] Removes existing feature or API Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/29ab115a7eb04aed848fc159d86683f2 ---

body.body: ### SUMMARY `PickleKeyValueCodec.decode` called `pickle.loads` on bytes read from the `key_value` table with no restriction on which globals could be constructed, so a payload in that table could execute arbitrary code on load. This applies the pattern Superset already ships in the `9c2a5681ddfd` key-value migration: a `RestrictedUnpickler` whose `find_class` raises `UnpicklingError` for anything outside an allow-list, with the codec translating that into `KeyValueCodecDecodeException`. ```python PICKLE_ALLOWED_CLASSES = { "builtins": {"bytearray", "complex", "frozenset", "object", "set"}, "collections": {"OrderedDict"}, "datetime": {"date", "datetime", "time", "timedelta", "timezone"}, "decimal": {"Decimal"}, "superset.utils.core": {"DatasourceType"}, "uuid": {"UUID"}, } class RestrictedUnpickler(pickle.Unpickler): def find_class(self, module, name): if name not in PICKLE_ALLOWED_CLASSES.get(module, frozenset()): raise pickle.UnpicklingError(f"Unpickling of {module}.{name} is forbidden") return super().find_class(module, name) ``` Containers, strings, numbers and booleans are reconstructed by the pickle machinery itself and never reach `find_class`, so only types needing a global lookup are listed. The encode path and the wire format of existing rows are unchanged — previously written rows still decode as long as they contain the value types Superset stores. Closes #8 ### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS New regression test `test_pickle_codec_rejects_disallowed_global` pickles an object whose `__reduce__` returns `os.system("touch ")`, decodes it, and asserts the decode raises and the marker file was never created. Before (fix reverted, test present): ``` $ python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/key_value/codec_test.py -q ........F.. [100%] > with pytest.raises(KeyValueCodecDecodeException): E Failed: DID NOT RAISE 1 failed, 10 passed, 1 warning in 0.77s ``` After: ``` $ python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/key_value/codec_test.py -q 11 passed, 1 warning in 0.77s ``` Also ran `tests/unit_tests/dao/key_value_test.py` and `tests/unit_tests/extensions` (255 passed) plus `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` on both changed files. ### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION - [x] Has associated issue: #8 - [ ] Required feature flags: - [ ] Changes UI - [ ] Includes DB Migration (follow approval process in [SIP-59](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/13351)) - [ ] Migration is atomic, supports rollback & is backwards-compatible - [ ] Confirm DB migration upgrade and downgrade tested - [ ] Runtime estimates and downtime expectations provided - [ ] Introduces new feature or API - [ ] Removes existing feature or API Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cb2799c898be44069ee8819c1f3c3af0 ---

body.body: ### SUMMARY Drops `pytz` from the two report modules in favor of the stdlib `zoneinfo`. Closes #3 Each call site needed a different replacement: - `superset/reports/schemas.py`: `pytz.all_timezones` (a sorted `list`) → `zoneinfo.available_timezones()` (an unordered `set`). A direct substitution would make the `OneOf` choices — and therefore the API validation error message that enumerates the accepted values — non-deterministic across processes, since set iteration order depends on the hash seed. The set is materialized once at import into a module-level `TIMEZONES = tuple(sorted(available_timezones()))` and used by both `timezone` fields. - `superset/reports/notifications/email.py`: `pytz.timezone("UTC")` → `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo("UTC")` for the `datetime.now(...)` stamp. Semantically identical here: for a fixed-offset zone like UTC there is no localization concern, and `tzname()` is still `"UTC"`, so subject-line date formatting is unchanged. Accepted-timezone set is a strict superset of the previous one — verified against the installed tzdata: ``` $ python -c "import pytz, zoneinfo; a=set(pytz.all_timezones); z=zoneinfo.available_timezones(); print(len(a), len(z)); print(sorted(a-z)); print(sorted(z-a))" 597 599 [] # nothing previously accepted is now rejected ['Factory', 'localtime'] ``` ### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS ``` $ python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/reports/schemas_test.py -q 34 passed, 1 warning in 0.44s $ python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/reports/ -q 145 passed, 1 warning in 5.14s $ ruff check superset/reports/schemas.py superset/reports/notifications/email.py All checks passed! ``` The issue's second verification command (`python -c "import superset.reports.schemas as s; ..."`) cannot import the module standalone on `master` either — `superset.reports.models` raises `Exception: App not initialized yet` outside a Flask app. The equivalent source check via `importlib.util.find_spec` passes: ``` $ python -c "import importlib.util; p=importlib.util.find_spec('superset.reports.schemas').origin; assert 'pytz' not in open(p).read(); print('ok')" ok ``` ### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION - [x] Has associated issue: #3 - [ ] Required feature flags: - [ ] Changes UI - [ ] Includes DB Migration (follow approval process in [SIP-59](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/13351)) - [ ] Migration is atomic, supports rollback & is backwards-compatible - [ ] Confirm DB migration upgrade and downgrade tested - [ ] Runtime estimates and downtime expectations provided - [ ] Introduces new feature or API - [ ] Removes existing feature or API Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/b79c2813999c483bb4dc09b2c64d3161 ---

body.body: ### SUMMARY Replaces `pytz` with the stdlib `zoneinfo` in `superset/tasks/cron_util.py`. ```py - tz = pytz_timezone(timezone) # UnknownTimeZoneError -> pytz_timezone("UTC") - utc = pytz_timezone("UTC") + tz: tzinfo = ZoneInfo(timezone) # (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError) -> timezone.utc + utc = timezone.utc ``` Semantics notes, since this is the call site where a naive swap is dangerous: - The function only ever attaches a timezone via `datetime.astimezone(tz)`, never by constructing a datetime with `tzinfo=tz` directly. That is exactly the pattern where `pytz`'s LMT-offset footgun does not apply, so no `localize()`/`normalize()` equivalent is needed — `ZoneInfo` resolves the offset from the datetime, which is the desired behaviour for windows spanning a DST boundary. The existing summer/winter (DST) parametrisations in `tests/unit_tests/tasks/test_cron_util.py` cover this and pass unchanged. - Fallback: `pytz` raises `UnknownTimeZoneError` for a bad name; `ZoneInfo` raises `ZoneInfoNotFoundError` for an unknown key and `ValueError` for a structurally invalid key (e.g. absolute or `..`-containing paths), so both are caught. The warning message and the UTC fallback are unchanged. - Fallback uses `datetime.timezone.utc` rather than `ZoneInfo("UTC")` so the fallback path cannot itself fail on a system without a tz database. - Output is unchanged: `schedule.astimezone(utc).replace(tzinfo=None)` still yields naive UTC datetimes, which is what the caller and the persisted schedule expect. - `datetime.timezone` is imported as `dt_timezone` because the function parameter is named `timezone`. Closes #2 ### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS ``` $ python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/tasks/test_cron_util.py -q 36 passed, 1 warning in 0.44s ``` `pre-commit run --files superset/tasks/cron_util.py` passes (mypy, ruff, pylint). ### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION - [x] Has associated issue: #2 - [ ] Required feature flags: - [ ] Changes UI - [ ] Includes DB Migration (follow approval process in [SIP-59](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/13351)) - [ ] Migration is atomic, supports rollback & is backwards-compatible - [ ] Confirm DB migration upgrade and downgrade tested - [ ] Runtime estimates and downtime expectations provided - [ ] Introduces new feature or API - [ ] Removes existing feature or API Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/081c24c00d994ca3a8df78813277c419 ---
